:::{#exm-zip-pmf}

#### Zero-inflated Poisson probabilities for the first few counts

Suppose that at some covariate pattern and exposure,
a zero-inflated Poisson regression model (@def-zip-reg)
has $\pi = 0.3$ and $\mu_0 = 2$.
The code below applies @thm-zip-pmf to the counts 0 through 3,
and compares the result with a direct mixture of the two arms:

```{r}
#| label: exm-zip-pmf-calc
zip_pi <- 0.3
zip_mu0 <- 2
zip_y <- 0:3
zip_pmf <- ifelse(
  zip_y == 0,
  zip_pi + (1 - zip_pi) * exp(-zip_mu0),
  (1 - zip_pi) * zip_mu0^zip_y * exp(-zip_mu0) / factorial(zip_y)
)
zip_mixture <- zip_pi * (zip_y == 0) + (1 - zip_pi) * dpois(zip_y, zip_mu0)
```

The probabilities of 0, 1, 2 and 3 events are
`r paste(round(zip_pmf, 3), collapse = ", ")`,
and the direct mixture gives
`r paste(round(zip_mixture, 3), collapse = ", ")`,
so the two agree.

:::
